page: Amazon Web Services m6id.32xlarge is a general-purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Powered by dedicated 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processors, it delivers 64 physical cores across 128 virtual CPUs with hyper-threading enabled. System memory totals 512 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware features include 54 MB of L3 cache, AVX-512 extensions, vector AES encryption instructions, and Total Memory Encryption. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 50 Gbps, and the server includes 7,600 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD instance storage.

Benchmark data demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded processing and memory bandwidth efficiency. PassMark CPU tests, extended instruction sets, and CPU encryption benchmarks reach top 10 percent overall performance. Multi-core workloads across stress-ng and Geekbench score in the top 25 percent, matching strong results in software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and static web serving throughput at 72.01 GB/sec. Large block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 333.37 GB/sec, supporting fast state access in data processing. Redis SET operations perform at 106.58 million operations per second.

The primary architectural tradeoff involves single-core execution speed. Single-threaded benchmarks, including gzip compression and single-core stress-ng tests, perform in the middle 50 percent relative to cloud servers overall. Cost efficiency relies on resource density: combining 128 vCPUs with 512 GB RAM and high-capacity local NVMe storage eliminates the overhead and latency of detached network volumes for intensive IO processes.

Amazon Web Services m6id.32xlarge is suited for scaling self-hosted relational databases, Redis caching layers, software compilation clusters, high-concurrency web serving, and ETL workflows requiring rapid scratch space storage.
